problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨6-{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}-6,\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨5-\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-t),\,\sqrt{6-t},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}f(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 2}\,(6-{t}^{3}),\,{lim}_{t\to 2}\,({t}^{2}-6),\,{lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{2}{{t}^{3}}⟩ \\  & =⟨6-{2}^{3},{2}^{2}-6,\frac{2}{{2}^{3}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-2,\frac{1}{4}⟩ \\ {lim}_{t\to 2}g(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 2}\,(5-\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-t)),\,{lim}_{t\to 2}\,\sqrt{6-t},\,{lim}_{t\to 2}\,(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨5-\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2),\sqrt{6-2},2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)+{lim}_{t\to 2}g(t) \\  & =⟨-2,-2,\frac{1}{4}⟩+⟨5,2,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-2+5,-2+2,\frac{1}{4}+4⟩ \\  & =⟨3,0,\frac{17}{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
